  PROBLEM: The read-result stages invalidate recorded security and validation runs only when the sync required conflict resolution, so a clean sync that advances the branch can leave a verdict for the pre-sync head eligible.

  PROBLEM: The dispatch error strings interpolate `ref` directly, so when it is `None` or empty the diagnostic can say "dispatched from None" or omit the ref.
  WHY: This can mislead operators triaging an exit-2 dispatch; MiniMax notes the empty-ref case is reachable if the default-branch read succeeds with an empty string.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py:lines 114-120 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: When `dispatched_ref` is set, the new-runs filter drops runs whose `head_branch` is missing or null, including a run that may have been started by this dispatch.
  WHY: The helper can time out despite the correct run being present; MiniMax rated this MAJOR while Qwen rated it NIT.

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: lines 19, 71, 78 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Steps 9 and 10 only discard recorded runs if the step 2 sync required conflict resolution, failing to invalidate a clean merge or fast-forward that advances the branch.
  WHY: A security or validation gate can pass on an older commit while the project branch tip contains unaudited and unvalidated default-branch changes.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: PR description: "An audit of an older commit could then stand in for code it never saw. ... A read-result stage now notes the project head it finds on origin before its sync merge. It reads a run's verdict only when the log shows both the project branch and that head as the commit covered ... A mismatch, or a sync that needed a conflict resolution, triggers one re-dispatch, and a second mismatch stops the project at Status: BLOCKED."
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md steps 2, 9, 10 and .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Evidence of absence: Step 2 only records "pre-sync head" and "whether this sync needed a conflict resolution" rather than tracking whether the sync advanced the branch or comparing post-sync HEAD; step 9 and step 10 only invalidate runs when the sync needed conflict resolution ("A step 2 sync that needed a conflict resolution changed the project's code after every recorded run, so none of them counts."), failing to invalidate when a clean merge or fast-forward advances the project branch tip beyond the pre-sync head.
  severity=critical
  confidence=5

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: line 19 (step 2 sync bullet); line 71 (step 9 invalidation rule); line 78 (step 10 invalidation rule) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Steps 9 and 10 invalidate runs only after a conflict-resolved sync, so a clean merge that advances the branch can leave a verdict for the pre-sync SHA eligible.
  WHY: The merged tree can contain unaudited default-branch commits even though the recorded run's SHA matches the pre-sync head.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py: lines 288, 306 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The error strings interpolate `ref` directly, so `None` or `""` can appear in the dispatch error message.
  WHY: An operator triaging a failed dispatch may be misled about the ref; this is reachable if the default-branch read succeeds with an empty string.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py: line 120 (`and (dispatched_ref is None or run.get("head_branch") == dispatched_ref)`) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When `dispatched_ref` is set, the filter excludes runs whose `head_branch` is missing or null, even when the run may have been started by this dispatch.
  WHY: The helper can time out despite GitHub having started the run with the correct ref, leaving the caller with exit 2 and no `run_id`.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: PR description, "It fixes security finding #5841 (A08, high): when `dispatch_workflow.py` could not name a dispatch's run, `/implement-plan-claude` steps 9 and 10 accepted the first completed candidate whose log named the project branch. An audit of an older commit could then stand in for code it never saw." and changelog lead, "Steps 9 and 10 used to accept the first completed candidate whose log named the project branch. ... an older audit of the same branch could therefore stand in for code it never saw (issue #5841)."
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md step 2 (recording), step 9 (security verdict acceptance), and step 10 (validation verdict acceptance), and the matching twin .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Evidence of absence: Step 2 records the pre-sync head and "whether this sync needed a conflict resolution" but does not record the post-sync head or whether the branch advanced. Step 9 reads "A step 2 sync that needed a conflict resolution changed the project's code after every recorded run, so none of them counts." — this is the only invalidation rule, and a `git merge --no-edit origin/<default>` that creates a new merge commit on the project branch without a conflict falls outside it. Step 10 mirrors the same narrow rule ("a conflict-resolved sync means no run counts"). agents.md (lines 1155-1160) describes the same narrow anchor. The intended fix therefore stops short of the named threat: a recorded run's `<sha>` can match the pre-sync head while the post-sync tree contains unaudited default-branch commits brought in by a clean merge. Changelog lead mirrors the same narrow rule ("a sync that needed a conflict resolution ... triggers one re-dispatch"). Five of the six pass-1 reviewers flagged this gap.
  severity=critical
  confidence=5
